title: How to Get Birth Certificate Online - Complete Guide
meta_description: Free registration if within 21 days. After that: affidavits, police visits, and 20-30 days minimum. State variations matter.

hero.one_liner: Apply for birth certificate online within 21 days for free or complete delayed registration with this complete guide

sections.heading: What is Birth Certificate & Why You Need It
content: A birth certificate is an official government document that records the birth of a child. It's one of the most important documents in your life - you'll need it for school admission, getting a passport, opening a bank account, employment, marriage registration, and numerous other purposes. The certificate contains essential information: child's name, date and place of birth, parents' names, and is issued by the local municipal corporation or village authority where the birth occurred. In India, birth registration is not compulsory by law, but obtaining a certificate is highly recommended. The process is divided into two categories: normal registration (within 21 days of birth) which is completely free, and delayed registration (after 21 days but within 30 years) which involves some fees and additional documentation.

sections.heading: Eligibility & Who Needs Birth Certificate
content: Any child born in India is eligible to get a birth certificate. The parents or guardians can apply for it. If the child has reached adulthood, they can apply for themselves. For normal registration (free), you must apply within 21 days of birth. For delayed registration, you can apply anytime within 30 years of birth, but you'll need to provide additional documents and pay fees. If the child is over 30 years old and never got a certificate, special affidavit procedures apply. Adopted children, children born to unmarried parents, and children of NRI parents can all get birth certificates. There's no upper age limit for getting a certificate - even if you're 50 and never got one, you can still apply for delayed registration.

sections.heading: Register Within 21 Days - It's Free
sections.content: Birth registration within 21 days is free in most states. After that, you'll need a late fee, an affidavit, and possibly a magistrate order. Don't delay - visit your nearest municipal office or register online at crsorgi.gov.in.

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Process
content: FOR NORMAL REGISTRATION (Within 21 Days - FREE)

Step 1: Collect Birth Notification Form from Hospital/Municipality If your child was born in a hospital, the hospital will give you a notification form (usually called 'Birth Notification Form' or 'Register of Births'). This form contains basic details: child's name, date of birth, gender, hospital name, doctor's signature. If born at home, contact your local municipal corporation or gram panchayat to get the form. Keep this form safe as it's your proof of birth.

Step 2: Go to Your Local Municipal Corporation/Town Council Within 21 days of birth, visit the Municipal Corporation office or Town Council office in your area (the one in your ward/constituency). Bring the birth notification form, your ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN/Passport), address proof (utility bill, ration card), and your spouse's ID proof. Some municipalities have a dedicated 'Birth Registration' counter. Ask for the Registrar of Births & Deaths or Vital Statistics Officer.

Step 3: Fill Birth Registration Form The officer will provide you a Birth Registration Form (different from notification form). It asks for: child's name, date of birth, place of birth, father's name and occupation, mother's name and occupation, parents' addresses, witness details (if home birth). The form should be filled accurately. Any mistakes here will appear on the final certificate. Take time to fill it carefully.

Step 4: Submit Documents & Get Application Slip Submit the form along with all documents to the officer. They'll verify your documents, check that birth notification is within 21 days, and keep a photocopy of all documents. You'll get an application slip or receipt with an application number. This number is important - keep it for tracking and future reference.

Step 5: Collect Birth Certificate For normal registration, the certificate is issued immediately (same day to 3 days). The officer will inform you when it's ready. Collect it from the municipality office. The certificate is a printed document on official letterhead, signed by the Registrar. Collect multiple copies (at least 5-10) as you'll need them for various purposes. Cost is completely free for normal registration. FOR DELAYED REGISTRATION (After 21 Days)

Step 1: Determine Registration Category Delayed registration is divided into categories based on how late you're applying: - Category 1 (21 days to 1 year): Simple process, minimal additional documents - Category 2 (1 year to 3 years): Requires affidavit and police verification - Category 3 (3 years to 30 years): Requires
High Court order or affidavit with newspaper publication Check which category your case falls into based on child's age.

Step 2: Prepare Required Documents Gather all available documents: hospital birth record, vaccination card, school admission records, passport/PAN of child if available, parents' ID proofs, address proofs, marriage certificate (if applicable). For Category 2 onwards, prepare an affidavit (on ₹10 stamp paper) stating reason for delayed registration, child's details, and parents' declaration. Get the affidavit notarized by a notary or lawyer

Step 3: File Delayed Registration Application Go to the Municipal Corporation office and ask for 'Delayed Birth Registration' form. Fill it completely with all available information. If any information is missing or unclear, note it in the form. Submit along with: - All supporting documents - Affidavit (for Category 2 onwards) - Photocopy of all documents - Recent photos of child (4x6, color) - Original and photocopy of your ID proof

Step 4: Police Verification (If Applicable) For delayed registration beyond 1 year, the municipal corporation will direct the police to verify the information. Police will visit your address and confirm that the child was born in your house (if home birth) and verify parent details. Police report takes 5-10 days. This is a standard procedure and not suspicious - it's just verification.
Step 5: Pay Delayed Registration Fee Fees depend on how late you're applying: - Up to 1 year late: ₹20-50 - 1 year to 3 years late:
₹50-100 + affidavit cost - 3 years to 30 years late: ₹100-500 + affidavit cost + possible court proceedings Pay fees at the municipality office. Keep receipt for reference.

Step 6: Obtain Registrar's Order After verification and fee payment, the Registrar will issue an order approving delayed registration. For very late registrations (beyond 3 years), you may need High Court order. This requires filing a case in High Court with all evidence, which is more complex. Most municipalities handle this within their capacity for registrations under 30 years.

Step 7: Collect Birth Certificate Once the Registrar's order is issued, your birth certificate will be prepared. This usually takes 7-15 days. You'll be notified via phone/SMS when it's ready. Collect it from the municipality office. Get multiple certified copies (at least 5) as needed for various purposes. FOR ONLINE REGISTRATION (Where Available)

Step 1: Check if Your State Offers Online Registration Many states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Punjab) offer online birth registration through portals like CRSORGI (Centralized Civil Registration System - Online Registration & Issuance). Visit https://crsorgi.gov.in/ and check if your state is covered.

Step 2: Create Account on CRSORGI Portal Go to crsorgi.gov.in, click 'Register' or 'New User'. Enter your email and mobile number. Set a strong password. You'll receive an OTP on your phone. Verify and complete registration. Your account is now active.
Step 3: Fill Online Application Form Log in to your account. Click 'Apply for Birth

Certificate' or 'Delayed Birth Registration'. Fill in all fields: - Child's details (name, DOB, gender, place of birth) - Father's details (name, age, occupation, contact) - Mother's details (name, age, occupation, contact) - Reason for registration (normal or delayed) - Your relationship with child
Step 4: Upload Required Documents The portal will ask you to upload: - Clear scan of hospital birth record (JPG/PDF, < 2 MB) - Parents' ID proofs (both sides, < 2 MB each) - Address proof

(utility bill or ration card, < 2 MB) - Marriage certificate (if applicable, < 2 MB) - Affidavit (if delayed registration, < 2 MB) - Photos (< 2 MB each) Ensure all documents are clearly scanned and readable.

Step 5: Pay Online Fee (If Required) The portal will calculate fee based on registration type. Pay online via credit card, debit card, or net banking. For normal registration, fee is zero. For delayed registration, you'll pay as per state rules. Once payment is confirmed, your application is submitted.

Step 6: Track Application Status Your application is now in queue for verification. You can check status anytime using your login credentials. Status updates: 'Submitted' → 'Under Verification' → 'Approved' → 'Certificate Ready' → 'Collected'. You'll get SMS notifications at each stage.
Step 7: Download/Collect Certificate Once certificate is ready, you'll receive an SMS. In some states, you can download the certificate directly as PDF from the portal (soft copy is legally valid).
In others, you need to visit the registration office to collect a printed copy. Some portals allow download and physical collection both.

Step 8: Get Certified Copies Once you have the certificate, you can get certified copies from the same municipal office. Certified copy looks identical to original but is marked 'Certified True Copy' and signed by the Registrar. Cost per copy is ₹5-10. Collect multiple copies as you'll need them.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes to Avoid
content: 1. Not Registering Within 21 Days Despite Hospital Birth Many parents delay registration thinking it's not urgent. Once you cross 21 days, your registration becomes 'delayed' and requires extra documents and fees. If you have a hospital birth record, register within 21 days - it's completely free. This is the most common and avoidable mistake.

2. Incorrect Child's Name Make sure the child's name on hospital record matches what you put in registration form. Any spelling differences will carry forward to the certificate. If you want to change the name later, you'll need to go through a correction process with affidavit and court order. Decide the name carefully before registration.

3. Missing Address Proof Less Than 3 Months Old Your address proof (utility bill, ration card) must be recent (issued within 3 months). Old utility bills won't be accepted. If you've recently moved, get a new bill in your name or use a rental agreement as address proof. This is a common reason for rejection.

4. Not Keeping Original Hospital Birth Record The hospital birth record (a printed sheet from hospital with doctor's signature) is crucial for registration. Keep it safe from day one. If you lose it, you'll need to approach the hospital for a duplicate, which takes additional time and may have charges.

5. Wrong Municipality Office You must register the birth at the municipal corporation where the birth took place, not where you currently live. If you were born in Mumbai but live in Pune now, register in Mumbai. Registering at wrong municipality will result in rejection. Check your ward number and correct office before visiting.

6. Not Bringing Both Parents' ID Proofs Even if only one parent applies, both parents' documents may be needed for verification. Bring both Aadhaar cards or ID proofs to avoid rejection. If one parent is not available, get a notarized authorization letter (Power of Attorney) from them.
7. Mistakes in Affidavit (For Delayed

Registration) If applying after 21 days, your affidavit must be accurate and properly notarized. Mistakes in affidavit will result in rejection. Common errors: wrong date of birth, wrong parents' names, spelling mistakes. Get the affidavit drafted by a lawyer or notary to avoid errors.

8. Uploading Poor Quality Scans For online registration, if you upload blurry or incomplete scans, they'll be rejected and you'll have to reupload. Scan documents at good resolution (200 DPI minimum), in good lighting, both sides clear, and crop out blank spaces. Check before uploading.

9. Not Collecting Multiple Copies Many people collect just one copy, then need more later and have to wait again. Collect at least 5-10 copies from the municipality office immediately. Certified copies cost only ₹5-10 each but take 1-2 days to get. It's better to get them all at once.

10. Forgetting Application Number Always note down and save the application number given to you when you submit the form. If you lose it, tracking your application becomes difficult. Create a WhatsApp reminder with the application number or save it in your phone notes.

sections.heading: State-Wise Variations
content: MAHARASHTRA Maharashtra's Mahavitran portal is one of the best in India. You can apply online, track status, and download digital certificate without visiting office. For normal registration, the office contacts the hospital directly to verify birth details. Processing time is typically 5-10 days. The state also allows certificate download as PDF which has legal validity. KARNATAKA Karnataka's CRSORGI portal is well-integrated with hospitals. Hospital records are automatically fetched if the birth took place in a registered hospital. For home births, you'll need proof from ANM (Auxiliary Nurse Midwife). The state processes delayed registrations faster than most. Address verification is done online when possible. TAMIL NADU Tamil Nadu processes online and offline registrations. The state has strict document verification. If applying through CRSORGI, the state sends an automated message with status updates. Certificate can be downloaded as soft copy or collected from office. Certified copies cost ₹2 per copy (cheapest in India). DELHI Delhi's system is slightly different - registration is done at the municipal corporation office (not municipality corporation exists in other states). Birth certificate comes in a specific format. For online registration, Delhi Health Services portal is used. Processing takes 5-10 days for normal registration. PUNJAB & HARYANA Both states use CRSORGI portal. Haryana has a smartphone app for tracking applications. Punjab's registration offices are less crowded than metro states. Processing time is typically 7-10 days. Both states have simplified delayed registration procedures. UTTAR PRADESH UP uses both online (partially) and offline systems. Government hospitals in UP automatically provide birth records. Registration is usually done at the Gram Panchayat office (for rural areas) or Municipal Corporation (for urban areas). Processing takes 10-15 days. RURAL vs URBAN AREAS In urban areas (municipal corporations), registration is smooth and online. In rural areas (gram panchayat), the process is more manual. Rural registrations may take longer (15-20 days) as verification is physical. However, fees are same everywhere.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
content: Q: Can I get birth certificate if the child is already 10 years old?

A: Yes, you can get delayed registration for a child up to 30 years of age. However, the older the child, the more documents and verification required. For a 10-year-old, you'll need school admission records, vaccination certificate, Aadhaar, PAN if available, affidavit, and police verification. Cost will be ₹100-200.
Q: Is birth certificate issued for children born to unmarried parents?

A: Yes, absolutely. The child's legitimacy is not a criterion for birth registration. You'll need to provide both parents' consent and declaration. The certificate will list both parents' names if both parents consent. If only one parent's name is desired, provide their separate declaration.
Q: Can I change the child's name on birth certificate after registration?

A: Yes, but it requires a correction/amendment process. You need to file an affidavit on ₹10 stamp paper stating the reason for name change, get it notarized, and submit to the municipal corporation. Process takes 3-5 days and costs ₹20-50. You cannot change the name arbitrarily - there must be a valid reason.
Q: What if my hospital has shut down or lost records?

A: You can still get delayed registration using alternative documents: vaccination card, Aadhaar (if issued before), school admission record, passport, PAN, or affidavit from parents and two witnesses. The process becomes more like Category 2/3 delayed registration with police verification.
Q: Is digital/soft copy of birth certificate legally valid?

A: Yes, the digital certificate downloaded from CRSORGI or state portal is legally valid under IT Act 2000. It has the same legal status as physical certificate. Many institutions and banks now accept soft copy. However, keep both soft and hard copies for safety.
Q: Can NRI parents get birth certificate for child born in India?

A: Yes, if the child was born in India, you can get registration at the municipal corporation where birth occurred. You'll need both parents' passports, NRI status proof (visa/PAN), and hospital birth record. If parents are outside India, an authorized relative can apply on their behalf with a power of attorney.
Q: How many birth certificates should I collect?

A: Collect at least 5-10 original certificates initially. You'll need one each for: school admission, passport, PAN, marriage (later in life), employment. Extra copies help if one gets lost or damaged. Collecting extras now saves you the hassle of getting certified copies later. Q:

Can I correct father's name on birth certificate after registration? A: Only if there's a typo (spelling mistake). For substantial changes (adding/removing father's name), it requires court order and is legally complex. This is why you must provide correct information at the time of registration. Get the father's written consent before registering the child's name with his name.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions & Clarifications
content: Many applicants ask questions specific to birth certificate. Some common confusions: Can I apply online or must I visit in person? Most services now have mixed models - initial application online, verification offline. Check your district's e-district portal. How long is validity? Government certificates are typically valid for 5-10 years unless mentioned otherwise, though some public-sector employers ask for fresh certificates if older than 2-3 years. Can I get a duplicate after loss? Yes, duplicate certificates cost 50-70% of original and take

2-5 days. Can I apply in my spouse's name? No, certificates are personal and non-transferable. Each person must apply individually. Can I apply if I've recently moved? Yes, you apply for the place where you currently reside or have domicile rights, depending on certificate type. Can my agent apply on my behalf? sections.heading: Pro Tips & Insider Advice
content: Based on multiple interactions with birth certificate applicants, here are practical tips: Apply early in the month rather than month-end when offices are busier and errors take longer to correct. Keep all documents (original and copies) organized in a single folder - you'll need them multiple times. Take clear photographs of all submitted documents using a smartphone camera in good lighting - if office claims something was 'not submitted,' you have proof. Visit the office on Tuesday-Thursday when processing is faster; Mondays are busy and Fridays have limited staff. Befriend the office clerk or get contact details of the supervisor - one call can clarify status and prevent rejection. Always fill forms in black/blue pen, not pencil - pencil documents may be rejected as temporary. Cross-verify all details before submission: name spelling, dates, addresses must match exactly across all documents. If submitting via eFiling, keep screenshots of confirmation page showing reference number and timestamp. Track via reference number every week rather than calling - reduces dependency on office staff. For online payments, use debit card instead of credit card - debit transactions complete faster. If you suspect your file was lost, immediately file a written complaint with office head in triplicate - creates an official record.
